documents: Rickerich, Ross & Valle-Levinson (2022), Wave enhanced overtides in an idealized tidal inlet system, JGR Oceans 127, e2022JC018848 (published PDF, 19 pages)

entry.evidence: Whether wave processes enhance the typical overtide generating mechanisms or create new mechanisms remains unknown.

steps.action: Poses the open question of whether wave processes enhance classical overtide mechanisms or create new ones, noting that classical studies disregard waves.
steps.quote: Whether wave processes enhance the typical overtide generating mechanisms or create new mechanisms remains unknown.

steps.action: Takes from Nascimento et al. (2019) the field observation that wave bottom stress is coherent with enhanced quarter-diurnal velocities at Arcachon, established only as a correlation.
steps.quote: They effectively identified wave bottom stress as a new overtide generating mechanism.

steps.action: States three research questions: whether waves enhance overtides, under which wave conditions, and which tidal or wave processes are most significant.
steps.quote: it addresses the research questions: (a) do waves enhance overtides near tidal inlets?

steps.action: Designs an idealized barrier-beach/inlet domain scaled on Arcachon Bay in coupled ROMS-SWAN (vortex force), with three families: tides only, tides plus waves (varied height, period, direction, tidal amplitude), and waves only.
steps.quote: Three Families of simulations were run to study the hydrodynamics under (a) tidal forcing, (b) tidal and wave forcing, and (c) wave forcing

steps.action: Runs the factorial set of 6-day simulations over microtidal and mesotidal M2 forcing and wind-wave to swell JONSWAP spectra.
steps.quote: A total of 93 simulations were run (2 from Family 1, 90 from Family 2, and 1 from Family 3).

steps.action: Fits M2, M4 and M6 harmonics by least squares to days 4-6 of simulated currents at every node and defines a normalized overtide amplitude (NOA) and its domain average.
steps.quote: To simplify comparison with other simulations, overtide magnitudes were normalized by the amplitude of the semi-diurnal tide

steps.action: Compares domain-averaged NOA of tides-waves runs against the tides-only baseline: waves raise NOA up to about 138% (microtidal), ranked by wave height, tidal amplitude, direction, period.
steps.quote: Quarter-diurnal (M4) and sixth-diurnal (M6) overtides of alongshore and cross-shore current velocities are augmented in the presence of waves.

steps.action: Maps plan-view and depth sections of NOA for the tides-only and four selected microtidal wave runs, showing dependence of spatial pattern on period and direction.
steps.quote: NOAs are greatest over the flood and ebb tidal deltas, and near the barrier beach where the water depth is shallow

steps.action: Compares depth-averaged along-shore and cross-shore momentum balances at station M1 over one M2 period between tides-only and tides-waves runs.
steps.quote: In the along-shore direction, an oscillatory balance exists between local acceleration

steps.action: Checks the along-shore momentum balance at other locations (S3, T''), finding a similar balance except for NNE waves.
steps.quote: Exploration of the alongshore depth-averaged momentum balance at other locations with the domain show a similar dynamical balance as described above

steps.action: Proposes that, besides known bottom-stress enhancement, wave-driven currents expressed in the WEC and composite pressure-gradient terms interact with tidal currents to generate overtides.
steps.quote: Bottom stresses are known to enhance overtides, yet the interaction between wave-driven currents and tidal currents may be responsible for overtide generation.

steps.action: Decomposes tidally averaged WEC and composite pressure-gradient terms along transect T'-T'' and identifies bottom streaming, bottom stress and pressure gradient as the overtide-generating terms whose cross-shore increase mirrors NOA.
steps.quote: Results from Sections 3.3.1 to 3.3.3 suggest that wave bottom-streaming is the dominant non-conservative wave process generating overtides

steps.action: Uses the waves-only Family 3 run and the tides-only Family 1 run as references to isolate wave-driven currents in the tidal and tidally averaged velocity profiles at S1 and S2.
steps.quote: The wave-driven currents produced in Family 3 simulation aid in the understanding of the altered tidal velocities.

steps.action: Compares the simulated tidally averaged profiles with Longuet-Higgins (1953) mass-transport theory and with Wang et al. (2020).
steps.quote: assume the same form as the mass-transport velocity defined in Longuet-Higgins (1953) seminal paper on wave-driven flow

steps.action: Compares peak flood and peak ebb current profiles along the transect between tides-only and 6 s and 14 s NNE runs, linking flood-ebb asymmetry to bottom streaming and return flow.
steps.quote: The nearshore location of pronounced flood-ebb asymmetries from wave-driven currents are coincident with elevated NOAs

steps.action: Sets the wave-enhanced bottom stress result against Nascimento et al. (2019) field correlations and reports agreement, extending it with two new mechanisms.
steps.quote: this study confirms the enhancement of overtides through increased bottom stress in the presence of waves

steps.action: Fits exponential relations of binned NOA against tidal amplitude-to-depth and wave height-to-depth ratios across all Family 2 grid points and reports RMSE.
steps.quote: A series of exponential relationships emerge between NOA versus

steps.action: Compares the fitted relations with Parker's (1991) threshold for non-negligible nonlinearity and with the Anthony and Orford (2002) coastal classification.
steps.quote: non-linear processes (and overtides) cannot be neglected

steps.action: Keeps the claim that waves enhance overtides through increased bottom stress, wave bottom streaming and increased pressure gradients, the latter two new.
steps.quote: Process (a) confirms the results of former studies and (b and c) are identified in this manner for the first time.

tree.answer: Wave-enhanced overtides near tidal inlets, previously seen as a field correlation (Nascimento et al. 2019)
No; overtides are inferred by harmonic fits of simulated currents (NOA)
Identify whether and which wave processes generate overtides
Only loosely: classical mechanisms (bottom stress, advection) versus wave-specific terms (streaming, pressure gradient, vortex force); not posed as formal rivals
No distinct predictions derived; mechanisms are ranked by diagnostic term magnitudes
Conditions set in idealized numerical experiments (tides only, tides plus waves, waves only)
Partly: similar balances at other locations, in the alongshore decomposition and on a transect 1 km west (mostly not shown); no observational validation
Kept as best explanation within the model

end.claim: In coupled tides-waves simulations of an idealized inlet, waves enhance overtides in currents through increased bottom stress, wave bottom streaming and wave-enhanced pressure gradients, the last two identified as new overtide-generating mechanisms.

decisive_move.sentence: The decomposition of tidally averaged WEC and composite pressure-gradient terms along the transect isolates bottom streaming and the pressure gradient; without it the new mechanisms would not be named.

gates.evidence: The research questions and the Nascimento et al. (2019) result directed the design of tides-only versus tides-waves families (p. 2-3), but no specific hypothesis fixed which terms would matter. The claim that waves enhance overtides could have failed against the tides-only baseline (p. 7). The mechanism attribution rests on diagnostic term magnitudes and on profile shapes, with no ablation (e.g., streaming switched off) that could falsify it (inference). Nothing is reported as fixed before the runs.

imports.item: Craik-Leibovich vortex force formalism for wave-current interaction
Longuet-Higgins (1953) theory of mass transport and wave streaming in water waves
Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes solution with k-epsilon turbulence closure

novelty_claims.quote: Bottom wave streaming and the wave-enhanced pressure gradient are identified as new overtide-generating mechanisms
[...] new mechanisms in wave streaming and the increased pressure gradient
Process (a) confirms the results of former studies and (b and c) are identified in this manner for the first time.

limits: No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The simulation count is inconsistent: 92 in the abstract and Section 3.1, 93 in Section 2.1.1 (including the single Family 3 run). The model is not validated against observations in this paper; skill is assumed from COAWST. The momentum balance is shown at one station (M1), and several supporting checks are 'not shown': other locations, the alongshore decomposition, the transect 1 km west, and the 8-12 s N runs. Mechanisms are attributed from the relative magnitude of diagnostic terms, not from experiments that remove a process (inference). The authors acknowledge that elevated alongshore currents under short-period waves are not understood and may reflect bulk-parameter Stokes drift. Processes omitted: rotation, wind, buoyancy, infragravity waves, wetting and drying. Sub-claims: 'waves enhance overtides' (confirmed against the tides-only baseline within the model); exponential NOA versus A/h and H/h relations (regularity_in_range, within the simulated parameter space and a single morphology). Minor text errors: Section 3.4 refers to 'Section 4.2' for the momentum balance, and the Figure 3 caption repeats '(c and f)'. Composition is none_fits: this is a set-condition numerical parameter study followed by diagnostic attribution. It has no crucial test among rivals (not strong_inference) and is not a trace series or nature's repetition. It is not exploration_first, because the question is posed first.
